native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB:
## Hypothesis (deliverable, ≈ 220 words)

Reframed outcome. The on-disk file has no late-life BA-degree column, so the question is addressed on `Highest grade completed, 1979` (years of schooling completed by age ~19; only 37 of 12,686 already at grade ≥ 16, so BA-by-1979 is treated as a footnote, not the headline).

What changes when academic characteristics enter. SES — composite of standardized log-income waves (1979/85/89) averaged with standardized log-family-wealth waves (1985/90/96, shifted by 1,011,901 so debts remain log-able) — falls from **β = +0.2343** grades per SES-SD in M1 (`grade ~ SES + Black + Hispanic + sex + age_1979 + family_size + mother_ed`) to **β = +0.1364** in M2 after adding the four ASVAB subtests (Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge), a **42% reduction** (range –35% to –48% across five specifications); partial F for the ASVAB block = 368.8 on (4, 9179), p ≈ 0. This is the standard partial-mediation signature: academic characteristics carry a substantial share of the SES→schooling association.

The racial pattern is the opposite of mediation: the Black coefficient goes from +0.0664 (M1) to **+0.1898** (M2), Hispanic from +0.0580 to **+0.4528**, while R² rises 0.6478→0.6966 — ASVAB correlates more strongly with schooling among the Non-Black Non-Hispanic reference (already a heterogeneous category that includes white and Asian-origin respondents) so conditioning on it *amplifies* the conditional racial coefficient rather than reducing it. Sex and family-size coefficients stay near zero, MomEd shrinks –49% alongside SES (parental education partly redundant with SES composite).

Caveats. (i) Outcome is schooling-by-age-~19, not eventual bachelor's attainment; the gap-formation period rather than the full lifetime. (ii) Causal identification is not possible — race, parental education, prior-year income and ability measures are all jointly determined by family background. (iii) Reference category 3 (Non-Black Non-Hispanic) lumps white and other respondents, so Black/Hispanic coefficients cannot be read as "Black-vs-White" gaps. (iv) Wealth waves have 67–87% missingness; the wealth-shift (1,011,901) is large. (v) Listwise n = 9,191 by M2 — inference targets the observed-on-ASVAB+wealth+parental-ed sub-sample; an imputation sensitivity on n = 12,532 yields a small *negative* M1 Black coefficient (–0.10) that ASVAB then pushes near zero, while the rational-pattern headline (negative raw gap, conditional gap reduced/eliminated by SES, suppressed-not-mediated by ASVAB) is robust across all specifications.
